My land is all wheat-maize rotation — that's just how it's done here in Quzhou, and it's how my family has farmed this ground for a long time. The same 10.1 mu grows wheat through the winter, then maize in the summer. I've been doing this cycle for 20 years and I know my fields.

**Wheat (plant October, harvest June):**
I'll use Jimai 22 — that variety has done right by me and by my neighbors. Before planting I'll do rotary tillage to work in last season's maize stubble. I put down base fertilizer with the diammonium phosphate and potash, then top-dress with urea at the green-up stage. I irrigate four times: once before sowing to get good germination, once in winter before it freezes hard, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. I can't afford to let a dry spring ruin the crop. For pesticides, I spray herbicide in the winter, then fungicide when I see the powdery mildew risk in spring, and one more time for aphids before heading. That's three sprays. I expect around 450 jin per mu — maybe more in a good year.

**Maize (plant June, harvest October):**
Right after wheat harvest I get the maize in fast. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as most people in the village. I do rotary tillage to break up the soil and chop the wheat straw. I put base fertilizer down and then side-dress nitrogen at the big bell stage — that's when the maize really needs it. I irrigate three times: at seedling stage, at silking, and once more if the August gets dry. Two pesticide sprays — herbicide early on, and one treatment for corn borer if I see it. Yield should be around 550 jin per mu.

With some family off-farm, I can't rely entirely on outside income. I need both crops to produce well. I won't cut corners on fertilizer or water.
